jscontroller="zYmgkd" data-sfc-root="c" jsuid="yQXyGe_1h" data-sfc-cb="">The Tick:<!--TgQPHd|[]--></strong> A laser is precisely locked onto this color. When the laser's frequency matches the atom's exact absorption color, the atom changes energy states. This provides a steady, ultra-high-speed "tick" that the clock uses to measure time.<!--TgQPHd|[]--></span><span jsuid="yQXyGe_1i" class="WBgIic notranslate" jsaction="rcuQ6b:&amp;yQXyGe_1i|npT2md" jscontroller="XqmSxe" data-sfc-root="c" data-wiz-uids="yQXyGe_1j,yQXyGe_1k" data-sfc-cb=""><span class="NMq1me" data-animation-atomic="" data-wiz-attrbind="class=yQXyGe_1i/TKHnVd"><span aria-hidden="true">&nbsp;</span><!--qkimaf yQXyGe_1i/HugV6--><!--cqw1tb yQXyGe_1i/HugV6--><button jsuid="yQXyGe_1k" tabindex="0" data-amic="true" data-icl-uuid="5ca2fd84-6360-4ff0-99da-2a390f343be0" aria-label="National Institute of Standards and Technology (.gov) (+3) - The Fano plane is a configuration of seven points and seven lines, where the circle counts as one of the â€œlinesâ€. Every point lies on three lines, every line contains three points, any two points lie on a unique line, and any two lines intersect in a unique point. The Fano plane can be constructed from scratch by using the binary representations of the numbers 1 up to 7, namely 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110, and 111. Three numbers lie on the same line if and only if applying XOR (â€œexclusive orâ€) to any two of the numbers gives the third number. More precisely, the ticket numbers are generated from the diagram above, which contains five triangles: three copies of the Fano plane, and two other triangular figures. The 21 tickets in the rightmost three columns in the winning list directly correspond to the 21 lines in the three copies of the Fano plane.
